newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa prepares for crucial Zairean peace talks.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa prepares for crucial Zairean peace talks.

text.p: Preparations for the first peace talks between Zaire's warring sides went ahead in South Africa on Thursday despite the rebels' swift rejection of the government's latest offer of a share of power.

Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko's special envoy arrived in South Africa in the late afternoon ahead of the crucial face to face talks with the rebels, who have seized control of a quarter of the central African country in six months.

Honore Ngbanda, Mobutu's security adviser and chairman of the eight-member government negotiations team, refused comment on the rebels' flat rejection of an offer of six cabinet posts in a government headed by new Prime Minister Etienne Tshisekedi.

"I didn't come here for that. We came here to talk, and good talks for responsible men do not take place by means of press communiques but around the negotiating table," Ngbanda, speaking in French, told reporters.

A plane carrying a negotiations team from the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, led by Bizima Karaha, rebel foreign affairs commissioner, left Goma in eastern Zaire on Thursday afternoon.
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila's team was expected to arrive late on Thursday at an undisclosed airfield near Johannesburg.
But it was unclear, given the rebels' flat rejection of Kinshasa's powersharing offer, whether peace talks would get off the ground on Saturday as proposed.
Zaire's full negotiating delegation, which comprises opposition politicians and a military expert, did not accompany Ngbanda to South Africa.

Kabila's advance party apparently numbered only two people, Karaha and information commissioner Raphael Nghenda. South Africa's Foreign Ministry refused to give any details about the arrival of Kabila's representatives.

South African Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad and the joint U.N. and Organisation of African Unity envoy, Mohamed Sahnoun, met in Pretoria earlier to discuss arrangements for the peace talks which were likely to be made public on Friday, the Foreign Ministry said.

According to news reports in South Africa the two sides are expected to meet on Saturday in Pretoria or Johannesburg, both in the heartlands Gauteng province but no precise schedule, date or location has been announced.

Ngabanda did not say when negotiations would begin, commenting only that: "I have come first of all to meet Mr. Sahnoun and the South African authorities to fix the date of the official start of negotiations."

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Wednesday he was hopeful the Zairean government and the rebels could set a date for both a ceasefire and proper negotiations during their talks in South Africa.
